_doc: BUG/PI items: 'mutation' turns the reference product into the delivered (faulty) version; the gold patch reverts it. CR items: the reference implementation is products/<product>/changes/<id>/ (full files overlaid on the repo) plus optional 'edits'. 'tests' = hidden tests (all must pass), 'mvs' = subset handed to the agent (BUG/CR only). Expected outputs: products/<product>/expected (build.py --regen).

items.title: Transactions reaching the credit limit exactly are rejected as over limit
items.description:
Since the last release the nightly posting job POSTTRAN (program CBTRN02C) rejects some daily transactions with reason 0102 OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION although the account does not go above its credit limit.

Example: account with credit limit 1,000.00 and no activity in the current cycle. Purchases of 600.00 and then 400.00 arrive in the same daily file. The second one is rejected, but after it the cycle balance would be exactly 1,000.00, which is allowed.

Expected behaviour (unchanged business rule): a transaction is over limit only when current cycle credit - current cycle debit + transaction amount is greater than the account credit limit. Reaching the limit exactly is fine. Everything else in the posting run (rejects file, account and category balance updates, counters, return code) must keep working as today.

items.title: Valid card transactions rejected in the nightly posting
items.pi_description: Several customers complain that purchases they made with a valid card were declined in last night's posting run. Their cards were still valid on the day of purchase. Please investigate and fix.

items.title: Current cycle debit total has the wrong sign after posting
items.description:
After the nightly posting job POSTTRAN (program CBTRN02C) the field ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT on the account master has the wrong sign. Example: an account with an empty cycle receives a return of -50.00; after the run the cycle debit shows +50.00 instead of -50.00. Because the over-limit check uses cycle credit minus cycle debit, later transactions of the same account in the same run are also accepted or rejected wrongly.

Expected: negative transaction amounts (returns, credits) are accumulated into ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT as they are, so the cycle debit total stays negative; positive amounts go to ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT. The current balance is updated with every posted amount as before.

items.title: Accounts far above their credit limit after posting
items.pi_description: Risk team found accounts that went well above their credit limit after the latest nightly posting. It looks like the limit was not enforced for some customers, mostly ones who had returns this month.

items.title: POSTTRAN ends with RC 0 and reports no rejects although transactions were rejected
items.description:
The nightly posting job POSTTRAN (program CBTRN02C) ends with return code 0 and the job log says 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :000000000', but the rejects file DALYREJS does contain rejected transactions. Operations use RC=4 of this step to start the reject review, so rejected transactions currently go unnoticed.

Expected: the job log shows the real number of rejected transactions and the step ends with return code 4 whenever at least one transaction was rejected (0 otherwise). Posting results must not change.

items.title: Transaction category balances too low
items.pi_description: Finance reports that the transaction category balances are much lower than the sum of the posted transactions since the last release. Interest charged at month end is therefore too low as well. Accounts with many purchases are the most affected.

items.title: Very high interest charges after the monthly run
items.pi_description: Customers are calling about very high interest charges on their accounts after this month's interest run. Last month the charges looked normal.

items.title: Interest transactions lose the cents
items.description:
The monthly interest job INTCALC (program CBACT04C) writes interest transactions whose amounts are cut to one decimal: a monthly interest of 12.37 is written as 12.30, and the account balance is increased by the cut amount too.

Expected: the monthly interest of each transaction category balance is balance x annual rate / 1200 with two decimals (extra decimals are dropped, as before), and that exact amount is used both for the interest transaction and for the account balance update.

items.title: Customer balances wrong after the interest run
items.pi_description: After the month-end interest run, the current balance of many accounts looks wrong - some customers now show a balance of just a few dollars although they owed much more before.

items.title: Interest of previous accounts added to the next account's balance
items.description:
After the monthly interest job INTCALC (program CBACT04C) the account balances grow by more than the interest transactions generated for them. Each account seems to receive the interest of all accounts processed before it.

Expected: when an account is updated, its current balance is increased only by the sum of its own interest transactions of this run (one per category balance with a non-zero rate). The interest transactions themselves are correct and must stay as they are.

items.title: INTCALC abends for accounts whose disclosure group has no rate
items.description:
The monthly interest job INTCALC (program CBACT04C) abends with 'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP' (FILE STATUS 0023) as soon as it processes an account whose disclosure group (ACCT-GROUP-ID) has no interest rate defined for a transaction type/category.

Expected (as specified for the disclosure group file DISCGRP): if there is no rate for the account's group and the type/category of the balance, the rate of group 'DEFAULT' for the same type/category is used. The run must complete and generate interest transactions for those balances too.

items.title: Old cycle credits still on accounts after month end
items.pi_description: Since the month-end run some accounts still show the previous cycle's credits in the new cycle, so customers' available credit looks wrong in the online screens.

items.title: All interest transactions get the same transaction ID
items.description:
All interest transactions created by the monthly interest job INTCALC (program CBACT04C) carry the same transaction ID: the run date from the PARM followed by 000000. They collide when they are merged into the transaction master.

Expected: each interest transaction ID is the 10-character PARM (run date) followed by a 6-digit sequence number that starts at 000001 for the first interest transaction of the run and increases by one for every interest transaction written.

items.title: Account totals in the daily transaction report are cumulative
items.description:
In the daily transaction report produced by TRANREPT (program CBTRN03C) each 'Account Total' line includes the amounts of all cards printed before it, so the totals keep growing down the report.

Expected: an 'Account Total' line shows only the sum of the transactions of the card (account) printed just above it. Page totals and the grand total are not affected.

items.title: Daily transaction report does not reconcile
items.pi_description: Finance says the total at the end of the daily transaction report no longer matches the transactions listed in it. The report used to reconcile before the last release.

items.title: Account totals over one million are wrong in the daily transaction report
items.description:
In the daily transaction report (TRANREPT, program CBTRN03C) the 'Account Total' line is wrong for cards with large activity: when the total of a card reaches 1,000,000.00 or more the leading digits are lost (e.g. 12,345,678.90 is printed as 345,678.90). Smaller totals are correct.

Expected: account totals are shown in full, up to the size of the report field (999,999,999.99), like page and grand totals.

items.title: Reject transactions for inactive accounts in the nightly posting
items.description:
Change request for the nightly posting job POSTTRAN (program CBTRN02C).

Today transactions are posted to any account found in the account master, even when the account is no longer active. From now on transactions for inactive accounts must be rejected.

New rule:
- An account is active when ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS = 'Y'. Any other value means inactive.
- A daily transaction whose card resolves to an inactive account is rejected with validation reason 0104 and description 'ACCOUNT IS NOT ACTIVE' (written in the validation trailer of the DALYREJS record exactly like the other reasons: 4-digit reason code followed by the 76-character description).
- This check applies only after the card and the account were found (reasons 0100 and 0101 keep priority). For an inactive account, reason 0104 is reported even if the transaction is also over limit (0102) or after the expiration date (0103).
- A rejected transaction must not change any balance, the transaction master or the category balances; it is counted in 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED' and causes RC=4 like any other reject.

No other behaviour changes.

items.title: Interest run: no interest on credit balances, minimum interest charge
items.description:
Change request for the monthly interest job INTCALC (program CBACT04C).

1. No interest on credit balances. Today a negative transaction category balance produces a negative interest transaction (the customer is paid interest). From now on, category balances that are zero or negative get no interest: no interest transaction is written and nothing is added to the account balance for them.

2. Minimum interest charge. When the monthly interest computed for a category balance (balance x annual rate / 1200, two decimals, extra decimals dropped as today) is greater than zero but less than 0.50, the amount charged is 0.50. The charged amount is used both for the interest transaction (TRAN-AMT) and for the account balance update.

Interest transaction IDs keep being numbered consecutively over the transactions actually written. Everything else (rates, DEFAULT group fallback, cycle reset, record layouts) stays unchanged.

items.title: Add a transaction count line to the daily transaction report
items.description:
Change request for the daily transaction report TRANREPT (program CBTRN03C, report layouts in copybook CVTRA07Y).

Auditors want to see how many transactions the report lists. Add one new line at the very end of the report, directly after the 'Grand Total' line:

- columns 1-17: the text 'Transaction Count'
- columns 18-97: dots ('.')
- columns 98-112: the number of transaction detail lines printed in the report, edited with the picture ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZ9 (right aligned, thousands separators, no leading zeros)
- the rest of the 133-byte record is spaces.

The count includes every transaction detail line of the report and nothing else (headers, totals and separator lines are not counted). All existing lines stay exactly as they are.

items.title: Financial report shows 'Virginia Clients = 000'
items.description:
The financial report CBL0006 ends with the line 'Virginia Clients = 000' although the report lists several clients whose state is Virginia.

Expected: the last line shows the number of account records whose state (USA-STATE) is 'Virginia', as stored in the account file, with three digits (e.g. 'Virginia Clients = 008' for the shipped data). The detail lines of the report are correct and must stay unchanged.

items.title: Financial report totals do not add up
items.pi_description: Our accountant says the totals line at the bottom of the financial report (with lower-case names) does not match the account balances listed above it.

items.title: Last names garbled in the financial report
items.description:
In the financial report CBL0011 the last names are printed wrongly since the last change: 'WASHINGTON' is printed as 'Wwashingto', 'ADAMS' as 'Aadams'.

Expected: the last name is printed with its first letter as stored and the remaining letters in lower case: 'Washington', 'Adams', 'Van buren'. Amounts and totals are correct and must not change.

items.title: Account search does not find an existing account
items.description:
The account search program SRCHBIN loads the account file (sorted by account number) into a table and looks up account 18011809 with a binary search. Since the last change it prints 'Not Found' although account 18011809 is in the file.

Expected: when account 18011809 is loaded it prints 'User with Acct No 18011809 is found!', otherwise 'Not Found'. The account file is always sorted by ascending account number.

items.title: Account listing shows wrong balances
items.pi_description: Customer service says the account listing printout shows wrong balances for practically every customer. The other columns look fine.

items.title: Show the number of over-limit accounts in the financial report
items.description:
Change request for the financial report CBL0011.

Risk management wants to see how many accounts are over their limit. Add one new line at the end of the report, directly after the 'Totals =' line:

- columns 1-22: the text 'Over Limit Accounts = '
- columns 23-25: the number of accounts whose balance is greater than their limit (ACCT-BALANCE > ACCT-LIMIT), three digits with leading zeros
- the rest of the print line is spaces.

An account whose balance equals its limit is not over the limit. All existing lines stay exactly as they are.

items.title: Make the state counted in the financial report configurable
items.description:
Change request for the financial report CBL0006.

The report counts the clients from Virginia only. Sales wants to run it for other states too.

- The state name is passed on the command line after the program name, e.g. `CBL0006 Ohio` or `CBL0006 New York` (with the run script: `jobs/run.sh <data-dir> CBL0006 New York`). Everything after the program name is the state name.
- When no state is given, 'Virginia' is used, so existing runs produce exactly the same report as today.
- A client is counted when USA-STATE is equal to the given name (exact comparison, same upper/lower case).
- The last line of the report becomes `<state> Clients = <nnn>`: the state name as given (without trailing spaces), followed by ' Clients = ' and the count as three digits with leading zeros, starting in column 1. Example: 'New York Clients = 004'.

Headers and detail lines do not change.
